What it controls: Determines whether a date requires radiocarbon calibration and which calibration curve is used
MORA: cc=1, cc1="IntCal20" for ¹⁴C dates; cc=0 for calendar-age controls
Rationale: Northern Hemisphere terrestrial ¹⁴C dates were calibrated with IntCal20; already calendar-dated controls were not recalibrated

What it controls: Thickness of the sediment sections for which accumulation rates are estimated
Rationale: Standard Bacon section thickness; for Panther Potholes this value reproduced the archived Gavin chronology

What it controls: Mean of the prior distribution for accumulation time, in yr cm⁻¹
Rationale: MORA cores accumulate substantially more slowly; 10 yr cm⁻¹ reproduces the Gavin chronology and is close to the approximately 12.8 yr cm⁻¹ reported for Panther Potholes

What it controls: Shape of the gamma prior around acc.mean; larger values impose a more concentrated accumulation prior
Rationale: Broad rbacon default retained for MORA and Gavin setting retained for Panther Potholes

What it controls: Prior mean dependence between accumulation rates in adjacent sediment sections
Rationale: rbacon default retained for MORA; Gavin setting retained for Panther Potholes

What it controls: Strength of the prior around mem.mean; larger values impose the assumed memory more strongly
Rationale: Broad rbacon default retained for MORA and Gavin setting retained for Panther Potholes

What it controls: Depth intervals treated as effectively instantaneous accumulation rather than gradual sedimentation
MORA: Jay Bath: 87–105 cm; Log Wallow: 40–98 cm; Reflection Pond: 45–64 cm
Rationale: Prevents thick tephra deposits from being interpreted as long periods of sediment accumulation

What it controls: Distribution used to accommodate chronological-control scatter and potential outlying dates
Rationale: rbacon default robust t-distribution retained for MORA; Gavin settings retained for Panther Potholes

What it controls: Number of MCMC iterations retained for the posterior
Rationale: Default sampling was retained for MORA; Panther Potholes required the larger value for adequate MCMC mixing and reproduction of the archived chronology

What it controls: Posterior interval reported for the chronology
Rationale: Ages are summarized with 95% posterior intervals

What it controls: Maximum core depth included in the model
MORA: Jay Bath: 153 cm; no manual extension for Log Wallow or Reflection Pond
Rationale: Jay Bath was extended to 153 cm to retain its deepest macrofossil sample; Panther Potholes retained the Gavin model extent
